blocks.note: Contracts between stages are enforced at the boundary, so schema drift fails loudly in minutes instead of quietly in a quarter.

blocks.x: The build sequence is deliberate: contracts and identity first, the working decision slice second, the verification harness third — because a Fleet Management System — Industry Use Cases capability without its eval gate is just another unattended automation.

items: Diagnose (2-4 weeks)
Baseline measured and signed, the metric and owner named, the risk envelope agreed in writing.
Prove (6-10 weeks)
The pilot runs on real data with a control group — the gate review happens whether the news is good or not.
Industrialize (1-3 quarters)
Hardening, enablement and scale-out in that order — no rollout faster than the evidence.
Compound (ongoing)
The next decisions enter the same loop — the backlog ranked by measured value per week of effort.

blocks.x: Operators describe the change as boring, in the best sense: the platform handles the recoverable failures by policy, pages humans only on user impact, and every intervention is logged into the evidence trail automatically.
Adapters ship with the platform release and are versioned like any other artifact — a core-system upgrade is an integration test, not a surprise.
